I will keep my main land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation, because that is the most steady and familiar way for me to farm in Quzhou County. I know this system, I can manage the labor, and it matches our local water and weather conditions better than taking a big risk on a fully cash-crop year. Since it is the start of the growing season, the winter wheat is already in the field, so I will focus first on spring fertilizer, one watering at jointing, and watching for aphids and rust. After wheat harvest, I will put that same land straight into summer maize, using hybrid seed for stable yield, keeping fertilizer moderate so I do not waste money, and irrigating mainly at the key stages if water is available. I will also keep a small piece in spring peanut, because it spreads my risk, gives me some cash income, and is not too hard for me to manage. For peanuts I will control weeds early, avoid too much nitrogen, and watch disease in the humid period. I will keep inputs practical, not excessive, and I will rely on the crops I trust most.
